newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-BRING ON THE EXPERIENCED REFS, SAYS MAZZONE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BRING ON THE EXPERIENCED REFS, SAYS MAZZONE.

text.p: Cagliari coach Carlo Mazzone has called for only the most experienced referees to be used during key final matches of the Italian season after his team lost to Bologna on Sunday in a game riddled with controversy.

"With four or five matches left to the end, why not field the referees with more experience, the international ones," Mazzone asked after the 3-0 defeat in Bologna kept the Sardinian club in danger of relegation to serie B.
Club president Massimo Cellino could not contain himself after the game, saying that young referee Daniele Tombolini's decisions had made him want to throw up.
Bologna's first goal came after a clear foul by Kennet Andersson went unnoticed. Most players were frozen in expectation of the whistle being blown.
Television replays then showed Bologna defender Michele Paramatti had handled the ball in his goalmouth to bundle out a shot that appeared to have already crossed the line.
No penalty was given and Paramatti was not sent off.
"Bravo Tombolini," Monday newspapers quoted Cellino as saying. "I tried to see what number he had on his back because I thought he was wearing a Bologna shirt.
"It's a disgrace...It's enough to make you vomit. I have nothing against Bologna...but I want to play soccer occasionally.

"I don't know whether what happened will have a bearing on Cagliari's future but I bet it will weigh on the referee's conscience, if he has one. It's hard to play against a team and the referee and it's been the same all year."
The defeat left Cagliari 15th in the standings, two points clear of Perugia in the relegation zone.
